prerequisites: Model-based system engineering for critical systems (S3)

learning_outcomes.text: Detect potential problems when targeting embedded programs on different hardware architectures, requiring knowledge of: Specific features of multicore and multi-core processors; Major computer families and their differences (32 vs 64 bits, use of call stack, FPU, vector architectures); The impact of architecture on memory representation (integer representation sizes, alignment on memory words, etc.); The impact of local optimizations on execution time (caches, RAM, pipeline, prefetch, etc.)

Detect problems when porting a program on an embedded target. Knowledge of the specific features of multicore and multi-core processors. Major computer families and their differences (32 vs. 64 bits, use of call stack, FPU, vector architectures); The impact of architecture on memory representation (integer representation sizes, alignment on memory words, etc.). The impact of local optimizations on runtime (caches, RAM, pipeline, prefetch, etc.).

syllabus_topics: The memory bottleneck of Harvard/von Neumann architectures to the present day (SDRAM banks) and cache memories
bibliography: E. Grolleau, J. Hugues, Y. Ouhammou, H. Bauer, « Introduction aux systèmes embarqués temps réel, Conception et mise en œuvre », Dunod, 2018

F. Cottet, E. Grolleau, S. Gérard, J. Hugues, Y. Ouhammou, S. Tucci -Piergiovanni, « Systèmes temps réel embarqués - 2e édition, Spécification, conception, implémentation et validation temporelle », Dunod, 2014
institution: ISAE-ENSMA (École nationale supérieure de mécanique et d'aérotechnique)
